label: Chapter 36
english: The demons that preside over the passions of the soul i.e. anger persist obstinately until death; those that preside over the passions of the body withdraw more quickly. And other demons are like the sun that rises and sets, affecting only one part of the soul; but the noonday demon (i.e. acedia) generally envelops the whole soul and suffocates the nous.

For this reason the solitary life is sweet after we have emptied out the passions; then our memories are simple and the monk’s struggle is thus not to prepare him to fight,, but rather to contemplate the struggle itself.
